author: Staff Writer
title: Moody's upgrades school district's ratings - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Writer ,
5 hours ago MONROE COUNTY — Moody's Ratings has upgraded its long-term credit ratings for the Monroe County School District.
The implications of the upgrade include:
● Reduced borrowing costs since a higher credit rating typically translates to lower interest rates when the district borrows money for capital projects, such as school construction or renovations.
● Enhanced investor confidence because the upgrade signals that the district is financially sound and well-managed, potentially attracting a broader investor base.
● Improved financial flexibility since lower borrowing costs can free up resources for other critical needs within the school district.
"We are proud to announce this ratings upgrade. It reflects the hard work and diligent efforts of the district when it comes to fiscal management of taxpayer dollars," Superintendent of Schools Edward Tierney said. “Serving the students, families and citizens of the county by being fiscally responsible is a high priority and this shows we are meeting that challenge.”
Moody's Ratings is one of the major independent bond rating agencies that assess the creditworthiness of entities like corporations, governments and school districts.
The issuer and sales tax ratings for the school district were upgraded from Aa2 to Aa1. Aa1 is a high-quality, investment-grade rating indicating a very low credit risk. It is the second-highest rating category, just below Aaa. The "1" modifier indicates that the district is at the top of the "Aa" category. The sales tax rating specifically assesses the creditworthiness of debt secured by sales tax revenues.
The district's COPs rating was upgraded to Aa2 from Aa3. COPs refer to certificates of participation, which are a type of debt instrument often used by school districts. The upgrade to Aa2 signifies that the COPs issued by the district are also considered high quality and carry very low credit risk.
